A problem that's been around since even before Reddit existed is that people use downvoting as an "I disagree" button even if the person is just bringing an earnest alternative viewpoint and not being a jerk about it and just trying to discuss it, which I'm assuming is the kind of behavior we want to encourage to have various topics discussed without people being fearful of violating a sub's echo chamber. My suggestion would be that to downvote something, you should have to explain why. No drop down boxes with preselected options -- explain why it is a bad post and let the community see why. I guess the explanation wouldn't have to be publically tied to a user if the downvotes themselves are not, but it would let people see why something was downvoted, like if it was for personal biases or if because the person really was just shilling or off topic or whatever.

Maybe make the downvoat reasons visible to only the user who posted the comment. That way they can get feedback on why they were downvoated, but people can't just copy someone else's reason for downvoating.
This also makes this feedback much less likely to be perceived negatively

This is a really cool idea. I'd actually take it the whole 9 yards and also make only upvotes visible to the user who posted the comment. It lets you get feedback on what people think but eliminates crowd voting and also makes brigading vastly more difficult. The group brigading would have to just keep F5ing hoping that they've finally gotten enough downvotes to censor the comment.

edit Oh holy smokes. It also takes a bite out of the circle jerk SRS type meta subs. They'd be left running around quoting comments without being able to attribute a number to them. There has to be a downside to this idea but I'm not seeing it.

Horrible, horrible, horrible idea.

Best case, everyone gets a stream of comments saying "fuck you" or "." just so they can downvote. Worst case, trolls and spammers don't get downvoted at all because everyone is lazy.

There's no way this idea could work well.

I totally agree.

But in some cases I'd like an optional explanation box. Or some feature to drop a PM without clicking around.

Hm. If only we had a box to optionally input our comments on something that we may or may not have voted on…

(Joking aside, a PM shortcut in the hover-on-username thingy would be neat.)

Not-joking I think that 99.9% of the users don't send a PM every time they downvoat. But if there is an interesting article linked in a subvoat which is not nearly on topic, an option to tell the submitter why I downvoated it might help.
Agree with you. Came here to say it won't work because lazy people won't downvoat as much because people are lazy. This will lead to more junk not getting downvoated when it should.

Those people who downvoated you without commenting: yeah, you really, really don't want to read what they might write in a comment box. If they had anything worthwhile to add to the conversation they would have commented anyway.

What do you think of this?

People keep telling everyone to use upvoats and downvoats as "contributes to discussion" and "doesn't contribute to discussion" buttons. Everyone doesn't care and use them as agree and disagree buttons anyway, because that's the first natural thing to use them as. Why not embrace this and actually use them as agree/disagree buttons? You could then have downvoats contribute positively to the post/comment's visibility. Of course, with this system in place, we'd need a way to mark posts and comments as junk -- but we already have that: the Report Spam button. It could double as a "mark comment as junk" thing, contributing negatively to its visibility.

(Disclaimer: Copy-pasted this from my not-well-received IFV post. But no one bothered to explain why it would be a bad idea, so I still think it would be good.)

I like that you seem to recognize that things quite aren't as they ought to be but you seem to be kind of soft on the solution. Like your answer seems to be to just reframe everything so as to legitimize existing behavior. My thoughts on that are if someone goes through the trouble of explaining their position and you have a position that doesn't jibe, then you should explain why. It shouldn't even be viewed as a burden -- I would think any opportunity to sell someone on your ideals would be a plus and anyone who sees it as a negative is someone who is incapable of defending their position.

If you disagree with an idea the OP presented and you're willing and able to explain your position, you're going to do it in the comments anyway. Or you're going to upvoat a comment that already expressed your negative opinions against OP's idea. Sometimes you just want to express "I disagree" and move on with your life, which, under the system @Brosama proposed and I summarized in my comment, wouldn't silence OP and would promote discussion about it – more people would be able to see it and comment with counterpoints. Or maybe with more people seeing it, would shift the scales in OP's favor – the post's fate would not be decided by a few first downvoters.

EDIT: Perhaps it would be nice to combine these approaches – have disagreement contribute positively to post's visibility and require an explanation when reporting spam/junk comments.

I like this better. There is no learning curve or special etiquette required. Fighting the tendency to use the downvoat button as a symbol of disagreement can be difficult and this would remove that difficulty.

I'd rather see downvotes just done away with. If valuable content is upvoted it'll rise above the spam, trolling and circlejerk content anyway and if we are a responsible community and do our part to report rule breaking content it'll get removed. Downvotes are too often used to suppress unpopular opinions and didn't most of us come here to escape the hivemind circlejerk?
Then it just becomes Facebook, where people have no way of calling out shitposts without commenting, and any upvote brigades will go completely unchallenged.

The trouble is (like what's happened to my original comment) people downvote because they disagree with something. That just drives down alternative opinions. If Voat is meant to be an open forum we will have to accept that means freedom to say what you believe but also it means you will hear things you disagree with.
I hate low quality, karma whoring comments. The catch phrases that gather upvotes like flies around shit, I would hope the community could move beyond it but history shows us that's not going to happen. If we don't want those posts to rise we shouldn't reward them with upvotes.
Mods should be limited to only a small number of subs so that they can moderate properly and warn shitposters that their "contribution" is unwelcome.
I know this is wishful thinking (contributers that only put forward thoughtful comments and mods that fairly and firmly manage their subs) but what are we doing here if not trying to move forward?

Voat is not an open forum. Voat is a democratic forum. There's a difference.

In order to be truly open, to be truly equal towards all viewpoints, you'd basically have to become a chan - no indication of support or disapproval, no sorting of comments based on variable factors, no identifying information of who thinks what.

Voat (and reddit before it)'s purpose isn't to create a platform for a free dialectic of ideas. It's purpose is to create a free dialectic of content, of which views/opinions are only a very small part. Sacrificing the democratic and dialectical nature of Voat in order to install a sense of equality would abandon the core nature of the platform and turn it into something that it really isn't.

I hate low quality karmawhoring comments as much as you do, but I recognize that in order for Voat to truly be a place of meeting for all walks of life, we must recognize that large communities will naturally tend towards such content. The only alternative is to have strict content standards, which is exactly what's happening on Reddit - and it isn't working. Reddit failed because it abandoned this goal. Reddit stopped treating all ideas as 'valid until proven wrong' (which the votes represented) and started treating them as 'valid if they meet these criteria' (which the strict content rules and overly eager moderators represented). Any step down the path towards the second paradigm is a step away from the first, and that will poison the dialectic - in other words, it will destroy the intellectual sanctity of Voat as a platform for content creation and discussion.
While this would limit brigading and would presumably promote more conversation, I don't want to have to validate every thing that I want to downvote.
Why not just have two sets of up/down votes? One meaning agree/disagree and the other relevant/irrelevant. You could do it in a little compass shape, so it still looks visually appealing.
well for one we already have the downvoting system in place. We just need to change it so the voting limits are higher. 2k comment should be enough.
